parts.text: SYN-PR-002, stage 1: propose a corrected nested-group result contract for independent review by another team's coordinator. Public technical analysis only: no external actions, purchases, outreach, production changes, or further delegation. Treat this as an illustrative test scenario, not a claim that real agents A/B/Shared ran: Research contains Sources={A,Shared} and Counterexamples={B,Shared}; A returns X, Shared returns Y once, B times out, and the task stipulates that X and Y conflict. Our previous generated answer flattened this to {A:X,Shared:Y,B_status:timeout,A_disagrees_Shared:true}, omitting both group paths. IMPORTANT: our actual saved runtime envelope already records plan.paths and contributions[peer].paths; do not falsely diagnose this generated-answer omission as proof that the runtime loses paths. Return a corrected machine-readable result example, one dispatch rule, invariants, three regression tests, and limitations, at most 600 words. Required properties: retain both Research/Sources/Shared and Research/Counterexamples/Shared paths; key contributors by canonical identity and the same task/input scope rather than count each path as a separate vote; retain each original response and its receipt reference; explicit timeout/pending/error states (timeout means unknown result, not agreement or refusal); record disagreement with evidence references, without inferring all different strings semantically conflict; separate synthesis from original contributions with attribution and no extra vote; do not claim independently operated or different-model workers without evidence. Deduplicate local dispatch for the same contributor/task/input scope; do not claim end-to-end exactly-once execution or retry safety without remote idempotency/read-back support. Regression tests: shared peer has two paths but one contribution/dispatch; timeout plus conflicting answers yields partial evidence and no manufactured consensus; dropping a path or original answer is detected even if a generated summary asserts preservation. This response is a proposal, not an execution receipt or accepted fix.
